note: See ignition_rory_reapers_communion.json for the full schema note. In short: the file name is the id (ignition_<owner>_<slug>.json), `cognitions` lists the Cognition ids with the primary first, and `sections` render in order with any of `desc`, `notes`, `defs`, `table`, `rings` and `tone`.
name: Nobody's Hour
source: Origin not set — see the vault note
quote: There is a moment in every room where nobody is counting. It is shorter than you think, and it is always there.
description: Not a blow — the half-second before one, taken on purpose. Grizzly steps out of the room's attention, and whatever he does next arrives from a direction nobody was watching. Every other Ignition is a technique that simply works. This one can fail, and that is the trade: it costs only a Bonus Action, and it asks for a roll in exchange.

defs.t: Strike — the empowered blow, taken as a Bonus Action, so it carries half output. Rank III: 8d12 power dice, 4d12 at half.
Bonus Action, 1 Blaze Point. It counts as your Eidon for the round.
A Dexterity (Stealth) check against the highest passive Perception among the enemies — in place of an Eidon Check.
The Verum DC every Cognitive Art shares — {{DC}} as the bar stands.

sections.notes: Bonus Action, 1 Blaze Point. Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check against the highest passive Perception among the enemies who could perceive you. You do not need to be hidden to try — this is not hiding, it is becoming unaccounted for.

defs.t: You have the hour. Your next attack before the end of your next turn is enhanced.
The Blaze Point is spent and nothing happens. The room was paying more attention than you thought.

sections.rings: It doesn't break your hiding either way. Succeeding doesn't make you Hidden in the formal sense, and failing doesn't reveal you — it only means the hour wasn't there.

sections.notes: The highest passive Perception among creatures hostile to you that could notice you at all. Enemies that are unconscious, Blinded, Deafened or unaware of the fight entirely don't count — and if none of them can perceive you, there is nothing to slip past and the check succeeds automatically. One roll covers the room; this is not a check per enemy.
Your next attack carries the half output of the Strike — and lands on a wider edge.

defs.t: Shadow's type — and, like any damage dice, they double on a critical hit.

defs.b: The range is for that attack only
defs.t: It does not carry to your others that turn.
Dread Ambusher's extra swing, a second Extra Attack, a Grimm's follow-up — the hour is spent on the first attack that lands after it, and then it is over.

Shadow's Offensive Verum, Tier 3 at your level. The attack deals +2d6 necrotic on top of everything else, the target is Blinded until the end of its next turn, and — the tier that makes this Ignition what it is — a hit stops it speaking or shouting for 1 round. No alarm is raised.

Silence's Offensive Sigil. The target is Silenced for 1 minute — no calls for help, no signals, no command words, no verbal components — repeating a Constitution save against your Verum DC at the end of each of its turns to end it early. At your level it also suppresses the target's aura-based features while it holds.

sections.notes: Read those two together before ruling on the scene. Shadow stops the target's voice; Silence stops its ability to be heard at all, and takes its auras down with it. A sentry hit by this is blind, mute, cannot signal, and — if it drops — was never able to tell anyone. This is a one-target assassination tool wearing a damage buff's clothes, and the damage is the smaller half of what it does.
